summary: fix(bonusly): replace cursor with real pagination and client-side filter for org top
reason: GET /users?top_level=true has no server-side free text search. Pagination is offset-based via skip/limit, not cursor-based. Amended post-review twice (Greptile P1s on PR #1899): (1) the initial client-side filter only scanned the single page selected by --limit/--skip, so a match outside that page was silently missed or under-reported -- fixed by walking the full top-level population (looping limit=100 pages via skip until a short page ends the walk); (2) the 50-page walk (5,000-user ceiling) then had its own gap -- if a company has more than 5,000 top-level users, the walk would silently stop and return an apparently-complete-but-actually-partial result. Added an explicit truncated:true field in the JSON envelope plus a stderr warning when the cap is hit on a still-full page, so an incomplete result is never silently indistinguishable from a complete one.
validated_outcome: org top successfully supports skip/limit parameters for the plain listing, and --search now scans the entire top-level population rather than one page -- live-verified by finding a match that sat at the tail end of what was previously the only page fetched. A normal (non-truncated) --search run correctly omits the truncated field; the 5,000-user cap path was verified by code inspection (no company in the live test account has anywhere near that many top-level users to exercise it end-to-end) rather than a live reproduction.
